key_insight: TRACE-Router makes routing decisions at the task level, using the final task reward to better match how long-horizon agentic workflows are actually evaluated.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable deployment of cost-quality adaptive LLM systems for agentic applications, improving accuracy-latency trade-offs without manual task-complexity estimation.
method: Assign each task to one backend model at admission using a contextual bandit.
Pin all subsequent LLM calls for that task to the chosen model to keep routing consistent.
Update the routing policy from delayed terminal reward, jointly optimizing accuracy and latency.
evidence_signal: Across three agentic benchmarks, TRACE-Router finds non-dominated Pareto frontier points; on tau2-Bench it beats latency-matched interpolation by 7–8 accuracy points, and on Terminal-Bench it reaches 7.1 higher accuracy points than the strongest single model baseline with 36% lower latency.
watch_item: Because routing is pinned per task and trained from delayed rewards, performance may depend on stable task execution traces and sufficient terminal feedback to learn good policies.
paper_title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
